quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When you are ready to turn left from a two-way street, where should you drive?

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
On the left side of the centerline.

questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street, drive in the lane closest to the centerline. Start your turn just before your car reaches the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Turn hand-over-hand into the first available legal lane.

questions.question: When daylight starts to fade, what should you use to help others see you?
questions.explanation: When daylight starts to fade, turn on your low beams so others can see you. Only use high beams in an open area with no other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do if you are following a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can turn and change lanes faster than other vehicles. Give yourself extra space behind a motorcycle so you have time to react to any sudden moves.

questions.question: Under normal weather, road, and traffic conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.explanation: More distance between your vehicle and others gives you more time to react if another driver makes a mistake. Keep at least three seconds of distance under normal conditions. Increase this distance in bad weather, poor roads, or heavy traffic.

questions.question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: When there is not enough room on the other side for your vehicle to completely cross the tracks.
When the crossing is in a city or town with frequent train traffic.
When you are transporting two or more young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is not enough room on the other side for your vehicle to completely cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: A train can come on any track at any time from either direction. Do not stop your vehicle on the tracks. Always make sure you can completely cross the tracks before you start.

questions.question: If you see animals standing near the road while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see animals near the road. They may suddenly run or change direction. Animals often travel in groups, so there may be more animals you cannot see.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a downhill curve. What should you do?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
Start braking after you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You cannot see hazards ahead, and braking in a curve can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: What is the proper way to make a right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the centerline before turning.
Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach from the right lane, then move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Use your signal before turning to warn other drivers. Slow down and stay as close as possible to the right curb when approaching the intersection.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, what should you always do?

options.text: Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: Always look left and right to check for people or other traffic that may cross or enter your path at intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings.

questions.question: What is a distraction while driving?

options.text: Anything that causes you to take evasive action.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that causes you to focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distracted driving can happen anywhere and anytime. It can cause crashes that result in property damage, injury, or death.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. You must look over your shoulders to check your blind spots.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: You see a green light, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to show you have the right-of-way.
Wait until you can cross the entire intersection before entering.
Enter the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can cross the entire intersection before entering.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can completely cross it before the light turns red. Even with a green light, you can be cited for blocking the intersection.

questions.question: When traffic moves at 50 to 55 mph, you will have the fewest accidents if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than other vehicles.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other traffic on the road (as long as it is within the speed limit). Vehicles moving at the same speed cannot hit each other. Crashes often happen when vehicles drive at different speeds.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you start driving. Other important tasks to do before driving include adjusting your seat, fastening your safety belt, and securing loose items. Never adjust mirrors while your vehicle is moving.

questions.question: You are parking uphill on a road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels away from the center of the road when parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb. This way, if your brakes fail, your vehicle will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: Why is using a cell phone while driving a distraction?

options.text: You worry about the cost of the call.
It takes your hands, eyes, and mind off driving.
Other drivers pay attention to your call.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your hands, eyes, and mind off driving.
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because it takes your eyes, hands, and attention away from the road. Even experienced drivers increase their risk of a crash when using a cell phone.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: Use a low gear before going down steep hills.
Follow other vehicles closely for better traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Use low gear before going down steep hills on slippery surfaces to help prevent skidding. Keep more distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Avoid sudden stops. If you do not have antilock brakes, pump your brakes gently.

questions.question: You should remove snow, frost, and ice from which windows?

options.text: Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.explanation: Clear all snow, ice, and frost from all your windows and mirrors before driving. You need a clear view through every window to drive safely.

questions.question: You should allow extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:
questions.explanation: Keep extra distance behind motorcycles. They can stop faster than cars, and you need room to stop if the motorcycle brakes suddenly or the rider falls. Also, motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?

options.text: They warn drivers about tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They use vibration and sound to warn drivers that they are leaving the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They use vibration and sound to warn drivers that they are leaving the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create noise and vibrations to alert drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are drifting off the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic light.

questions.question: Strong wind gusts on highways:
questions.explanation: Strong wind can cause problems for all drivers, not just large vehicles. Wind can reduce visibility by blowing dirt and dust, and it can also physically push a vehicle off course.

questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close to the car ahead):

options.text: Cannot result in a traffic ticket.
Prevents being cut off and reduces collisions.

questions.explanation: Tailgating is dangerous and can make other drivers angry. It may lead to aggressive driving and legal consequences for unsafe driving.

questions.question: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic light means:

options.text: You may turn right after slowing down and checking for traffic.
You cannot turn right until the light turns green.
You may turn right after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn right until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must wait until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: You are in a minor collision with no injuries and little damage. You should:

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: After a collision with no injuries, you should move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: This sign warns that:

options.text: The right lane is ending and you must move left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending and you must move left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead. This sign warns that there will be fewer lanes ahead and traffic must merge left.

questions.question: When you see a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog crossing the street, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is safely away from your path.
Honk your horn as you pass them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is safely away from your path.
questions.explanation: You must stop for a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog until they are well away from your vehicle. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: On a one-way street, you may turn left onto another one-way street only if:
questions.explanation: You may turn left onto a one-way street only if traffic moves to the left. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the divided highway ends ahead. Be ready to change lanes.

questions.question: At a flashing yellow light, you must:

options.text: Wait for the green light before going.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution. Watch for crossing traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:
questions.explanation: If there is danger, honk your horn loudly. Do this when a child or any other pedestrian is about to step into the street in front of your moving vehicle.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction where this sign is posted.

questions.question: Make room for cars entering the freeway by:

options.text: Staying at your current speed and position.

questions.explanation: Make room for cars entering the freeway. If possible, move to the next lane to create space. If you cannot move lanes, slow down to let them merge safely.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction where this sign is posted.

questions.question: Stopping distances and crash severity:

options.text: Are not affected by vehicle speed.

questions.explanation: It takes longer to stop at higher speeds. Crashes are also more severe at higher speeds.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must choose to go right or left.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must choose to go right or left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road splits. You must bear either right or left.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on the left, it is safe to return to the right lane:

options.text: When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing another vehicle on the left, move back to the right lane when you can see the front of that vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Assume all drivers follow the right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow the right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you have the right-of-way. Always consider the situation at an intersection. Yield your legal right-of-way if it can prevent a collision.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than on a city street:

options.text: Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your vehicle.

questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for changes in traffic. Watch for signals from other drivers. Expect cars merging at on-ramps and be ready for sudden changes in road conditions and traffic flow.

questions.question: Reaction time is slower after:
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your ability to see clearly and makes you less alert. As you drink more alcohol, your judgment gets worse and your driving skills decrease. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and how other vehicles are moving.
